protocol: In-flight dyspnea began at a reported aircraft altitude of 28,000 ft after ascent and cabin depressurization. The 2023 author account identifies the 2018 MiG-29 incident. Cabin pressure history and exposed denominator are unavailable.
outcome_window: Onset in flight. The journal places Warsaw emergency department presentation 6 hours after emergency landing. Discharged on reported day 19 without residual neurological deficit. Longer-term follow-up was not reported.
locator: Case Report pp. 107–108 and Table I p. 108 (PDF pp. 2–3)
note: Selected single operational flight case with a clinical severe altitude DCS diagnosis by the treating authors. The proceedings and author account describe this same episode.
